links.outcome: Non-palliative in-hospital death after ML early warning system implementation versus pre-intervention and control units
links.effect: GIM deaths 1.6% v. 2.1% (adjusted RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.55-1.00); subspecialty 1.9% v. 2.1% (RR 0.89, 0.63-1.28); difference-in-differences RR 0.79 (0.50-1.24), CI crossing 1.
links.quote: Non-palliative deaths were significantly lower in the intervention period than the pre-intervention period among patients in GIM (1.6% v. 2.1%; adjusted relative risk [RR] 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-1.00) but not in the subspecialty cohorts (1.9% v. 2.1%; adjusted RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.63-1.28).

screen.reason: Evaluates the clinical impact of deploying a machine learning early warning system with real-time alerting to clinicians versus historical/unalerted controls.

primary.practice: real-time clinical alerting and early warning system workflow
